name: Protobuf Decoder
description: Decode protobuf binary data: list the fields from the wire format, or restore JSON with a .proto descriptor.

examples.label: Decode the same bytes with a .proto descriptor
examples.value: message Person { string name = 1; int32 id = 2; }

hints.input: Pick the right input encoding for hex or Base64; importing a binary file fills the box with Base64 automatically.
hints.mode: Wire mode only looks at the byte structure and guesses length-delimited values as text or nested messages; the .proto mode adds field names, declared types and an unknown field count.
hints.limit: Results are truncated — not rejected — once the field count or nesting depth limit is reached.

faq.q: How does wire mode tell text from a nested message?
faq.a: A length-delimited value is shown as text when it is printable UTF-8; otherwise it is parsed as a nested message; if neither works you get a hex preview.

faq.q: Why are field numbers used as JSON keys?
faq.a: Without a descriptor there are no field names, only numbers. Integers beyond the JavaScript safe range are emitted as strings so no precision is lost.
Google well-known types such as google/protobuf/timestamp.proto are available; other imports must be merged into the same descriptor file first.

faq.q: Decoding failed — what should I check?
faq.a: The error carries the byte offset. First confirm the input encoding, then confirm the field types in the descriptor match the actual data.
